name: Familial Restrictive Cardiomyopathy

criteria.description: Evidence of severe diastolic dysfunction with restrictive filling pattern on echocardiography or cardiac catheterization
Positive family history of restrictive cardiomyopathy or sudden cardiac death
Exclusion of other causes of restrictive physiology such as amyloidosis, sarcoidosis, or radiation-induced heart disease
Identification of pathogenic mutation in sarcomeric or cytoskeletal genes associated with familial restrictive cardiomyopathy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of diastolic dysfunction with restrictive filling pattern plus either positive family history or exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can support diagnosis but is not mandatory

pathognomonic.symptomName: Severe exercise intolerance due to diastolic heart failure
Biatrial enlargement with restrictive filling pattern

laboratory: Normal or mildly elevated natriuretic peptides (BNP, NT-proBNP)
Normal cardiac enzymes unless ischemia present
imaging: Echocardiography showing restrictive filling pattern and biatrial enlargement
Cardiac MRI demonstrating normal or mildly reduced ventricular volumes with preserved systolic function
Absence of late gadolinium enhancement typical for infiltrative diseases
genetic: Pathogenic mutations in sarcomeric genes such as TNNI3, TNNT2, MYH7
Mutations in cytoskeletal genes like DES (desmin)
other: Hemodynamic studies confirming elevated ventricular filling pressures with normal systolic function
Endomyocardial biopsy may show nonspecific fibrosis without infiltrative disease

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of amyloid deposits on biopsy
Characteristic late gadolinium enhancement on cardiac MRI
Elevated serum or urine light chains in AL amyloidosis
Multisystem involvement with pulmonary or lymph node disease
Patchy late gadolinium enhancement on cardiac MRI
Pericardial thickening or calcification on imaging
Respiratory variation in ventricular filling pressures

redFlags: Rapid progression of heart failure symptoms despite therapy
Family history of sudden cardiac death or cardiomyopathy
references: Maron BJ, Towbin JA, Thiene G, et al. Contemporary definitions and classification of the cardiomyopathies. Circulation. 2006;113(14):1807-1816.
Ho CY. Genetic advances in sarcomeric cardiomyopathies: state of the art. Cardiovasc Res. 2015;105(4):397-408.
